payload.parent_proof_nl: Let x be any real number. By the definition of the floor function, floor(x) is the greatest integer less than or equal to x. Therefore floor(x) itself is an integer satisfying floor(x) ≤ x. Since x was arbitrary, this holds for every real number x.

parent_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all real x, the greatest integer less than or equal to x is less than or equal to x.

payload.root_theorem_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

assembly_plan.proof_skeleton_nl: No meaningful intermediate lemmas were identified. The proof should remain a direct argument from the definition of floor: for an arbitrary real x, floor(x) is the greatest integer less than or equal to x, hence in particular floor(x) ≤ x; since x was arbitrary, the statement holds for all real x.
